items.title: Pyrefly: A Fast Static Type Checker for Python Projects
items.description: Learn how to use Pyrefly, a fast static type checker for Python, to catch type errors, generate type annotations, and measure type coverage.
items.summary: Pyrefly is a fast static type checker for Python that helps you catch type-related issues before running your code. It also includes features for generating type hints and measuring type coverage across a codebase.

items.title: Python Circular Imports: Why They Happen and How to Fix Them
items.description: Confused by Python circular imports? Learn why they happen, how Python's import system works, and how to fix import errors using practical examples.
items.summary: A Python circular import happens when two modules import each other and one of them isn’t finished loading yet. Python reports it as an ImportError or an AttributeError , usually with a message about a partially initialized module.

items.title: MCP vs API Calls: Which Should You Use for Python LLM Apps?
items.description: MCP vs API calls: build one Python tool, integrate it both ways, and compare. Learn what each approach costs and when an MCP server pays for itself.
items.summary: Anthropic open-sourced the Model Context Protocol (MCP) in November 2024 to fix a scaling problem: every new tool a model reached for needed its own integration, built on direct API calls. Building that integration today involves a decision usually framed as MCP vs API calls.

items.title: How to Get Out of Tutorial Hell
items.description: Stuck in tutorial hell? Learn how to get out by turning Python tutorials into practical projects that build real skills and lasting confidence.
items.summary: Tutorial hell is an unfortunate reality for many newcomers to Python, and learning how to get out of it starts with understanding why it’s so easy to fall into. When you’re a beginner, finishing tutorials is addictive!

items.title: Exploring AI Coding Agent Workflows
items.description: AI coding agents come in four types: IDE, terminal, PR, and cloud. Learn how each workflow fits into modern Python development.
items.summary: AI coding agents can read your code, reason about changes, and act on your behalf. To choose the right one, it helps to understand the four common workflow types: integrated development environment (IDE), terminal, pull request (PR), and cloud.

items.summary: Despite recent progress in dexterous reference tracking, existing models focus primarily on single-hand manipulation and a limited range of interactions, leaving the bimanual dexterous behaviors common in real life unaddressed.
